# `⋄` — Separator

At statement level, `⋄` separates expressions. A line break does the same.

```apl
x←2 ⋄ y←3 ⋄ x+y    ⍝ 5
```

Inside [brackets](brackets.qmd), `⋄` separates major cells. A trailing `⋄` builds an array from one cell. A single number is a cell of rank 0, so `[42 ⋄]` is a one-item vector.

```apl
[1 2 ⋄ 3 4]        ⍝ 2 2⍴1 2 3 4
⍴[1 2 ⋄]           ⍝ 1 2
⍴[42 ⋄]            ⍝ [1]
```

Inside [parentheses](parentheses.qmd), `⋄` separates rows, and the result is a vector of the rows. Each row reads as brackets do, so it is always a vector.

```apl
(1 2 ⋄ 3)          ⍝ [[1 2] [3]]
```
